newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin to give fiscal update on October 9.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin to give fiscal update on October 9.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin will deliver the annual update on Canada's economic and fiscal situation on Wednesday, October 9, the Finance Department said on Monday.
The update will contain the final figures for the fiscal 1995/96 (April-March) budget.

Martin has repeatedly said that the 1995/96 deficit would come below C$30 billion (US$21.9 billion). He is expected to undershoot his C$32.7 billion (US$23.87 billion) deficit target by at least C$2.5 billion, largely due to his leaving last year's contingency reserves untouched.
The budget update could also contain a preview of Canada's fiscal performance so far in 1996/97 and an outline of Martin's fiscal targets for the 1997/98 budget.
In his last budget, Martin set the 1996/97 deficit target at C$24.3 billion (US$17.74 billion).

The Liberal government has been using a series of two-year rolling targets for deficit reduction. Martin has pledged to bring the deficit down to 2.0 percent of gross domestic product in 1997/98, but has refused to set a deadline for balancing the budget.
